title: Apple's iPad Mini Set for Biggest Upgrade in Years With OLED Display, New Chip
excerpt: Apple's new iPad Mini will feature an OLED display, marking its biggest upgrade since 2021.
body:
Key Takeaways
  • Apple's new iPad Mini will feature an OLED display, marking its biggest upgrade since 2021.
  • Codenamed J510, the iPad Mini may launch by October 2026 with a starting price of $599.
  • Upgrades include a new chip, vibration-based speakers, and increased water resistance.
  • Despite the OLED upgrade, the refresh rate may remain at 60Hz, similar to the current model.
  • The iPad Mini's price increase could narrow the gap with the iPad Air, also starting at $599.
  • Apple is reportedly planning to launch a new iPad Mini with an OLED display by October 2026, according to Bloomberg's Mark Gurman, marking the biggest upgrade to the compact tablet since 2021.
  • The device, codenamed J510, would be the first non-Pro iPad to feature OLED technology, offering richer colors, higher contrast, and true blacks compared to the current LCD screen.
  • Additional rumored upgrades include an A19 Pro or A20 chip, a vibration-based speaker system, and increased water resistance — though the display may stay at 60Hz rather than adopting ProMotion.
  • The new iPad Mini could cost up to $100 more than the current model, which starts at $499, due to the premium OLED panel.

Apple's smallest tablet is set for its most significant overhaul in years. The next iPad Mini will reportedly feature an OLED display for the first time, putting it in line with the iPhone and iPad Pro in screen technology, according to Bloomberg's Mark Gurman.

The device, internally codenamed J510, could launch as early as this fall with availability expected by October. It would be the first non-Pro iPad to adopt the technology Apple has used in iPhones since 2017 and the iPad Pro since 2024.

Four Key Upgrades

The headline change is the switch from LCD to OLED. The organic light-emitting diode display allows each pixel to produce its own light, delivering deeper blacks, richer colors, and improved contrast ratios. For a tablet frequently used for reading, media consumption, and creative work, the difference should be immediately noticeable.

Beyond the screen, Gurman has previously reported three additional upgrades. The new iPad Mini is expected to receive a vibration-based speaker system that uses the display or chassis to produce sound, eliminating traditional speaker holes. This change would also enable increased water resistance — a first for any iPad model at this price point.

The processor is also due for a jump. The current iPad Mini runs Apple's A17 Pro chip. Its successor is rumored to ship with either an A19 Pro — the same chip in the iPhone 17 Pro — or the A20 Pro expected in the iPhone 18 Pro. Either would bring substantial performance gains, improved machine learning capabilities, and better support for Apple Intelligence features.

The 60Hz Question

One potential disappointment: despite the OLED upgrade, the new iPad Mini may retain a 60Hz refresh rate. Korean leaker yeux1122 reported that Samsung has begun mass production of the device's 8.4-inch "hybrid" OLED panel using LTPS technology, which supports only a fixed 60Hz rate — identical to the current LCD model.

Apple has historically reserved its ProMotion variable refresh rate (up to 120Hz) for Pro-branded devices, which use the more expensive LTPO OLED panels. While the company made an exception for the iPhone 17 this year, the iPad Mini appears unlikely to get the same treatment — likely a cost-saving measure to keep the tablet's price from climbing too far.

Price and Competition

The current iPad Mini starts at $499 for the Wi-Fi model with 128GB of storage. Given the OLED panel and other hardware upgrades, analysts expect the new model could cost up to $100 more, potentially starting at $599. That would narrow the gap with the iPad Air, which currently starts at $599 for the 11-inch model.

For professionals in India's tech industry and Indian students abroad, the iPad Mini occupies a unique niche — portable enough to carry everywhere, powerful enough for serious work. A significant spec bump with OLED could reinforce its appeal as a compact productivity and content-consumption device.

Apple is also reportedly working on refreshed versions of the entry-level iPad (codenamed J581, expected Q1 2027) and the iPad Air (codenamed J807 and J837 for the 11-inch and 13-inch models, respectively). The company plans to eventually bring OLED to the iPad Air as well, though the base model is expected to retain LCD screens to keep costs down.

With Samsung's panel production already underway, the October launch window appears solid. Apple's fall hardware event — typically held in September alongside new iPhones — could be where the updated iPad Mini makes its debut.
